examples.text: The process of unliming hides and skins in tanning has been a slow and disgusting one, consisting in soaking the skins in a bath of manure in water, called bate.

glosses: A vat which contains this liquid.

examples.text: […] and weares his Boot very ſmooth, like vnto the Signe of the Legge; and breedes no bate with telling of diſcreete stories:
So the strife redoubled and the weapons together clashed and ceased not bate and debate and naught was to be seen but blood flowing and necks bowing; […]
The other merely needs jealousy and bate, of which there are great and easily accessible reservoirs in every human heart.
What bate are you on now = where are you going and why ? The dog is on some bate = is finding or following a scent.

glosses: To soak leather so as to remove chemicals used in tanning; to steep in bate.

examples.text: The fiꝛſt is holde faſt at all timys, and ſpecially whan ſhe batith. It is calde batyng, for ſhe batith with hiꝛ ſelfe moſt oftyn cauſeles[.]

glosses: To reduce the force of something; to abate.

examples.text: Ah, left ſome Thorn ſhoul'd pierce thy tender Foot, / Or thou ſhoul'dſt fall in flying my purſuit! / To ſharp uneven Ways thy ſteps decline; / Abate thy Speed, and I will bate of mine.

glosses: To restrain, usually with the sense of being in anticipation

examples.text: […] and to his dying day he bated his breath a little when he told the story of the stroke with the willow wand.

glosses: To cut off, remove, take away.

examples.text: Also about Autumne bate the earth from about the roots of Olives, and lay them bare, but in stead thereof put good mucke thereto.
Nay, if he be of a proud humour, […] he will not Bate an Ace of abſolute certainty, but however doubtful or improbable the thing is, coming f[r]om him it muſt go for an indiſputable truth.
Bate the King, and be he fleſh and blood, / He lyes that ſaies it, thy mother at fifteen / Was black and ſinful to her.
Bate (I beſeech you) widdow Dido.
Bardoll, am I not falne away vilely ſince this laſt action? do I not bate? do I not dwindle? Why, my skinne hangs about me like an old Ladies looſe gowne.
When baseness is exalted, do not bate / The place its honour for the person's sake; […]

glosses: To lessen by retrenching, deducting, or reducing; to abate; to beat down; to lower.

examples.text: [W]hen the Landholder's Rent falls, he muſt either bate the Labourer's Wages, or not imploy, or not pay him; which either way makes him feel the want of Money.

glosses: To allow by way of abatement or deduction.

examples.text: Theſe are the conditions of his treating with God, to whom he bates nothing or what he ſtood upon with the Parlament: as if Commiſſions of Array could deale with him alſo.
